question: A 50-year-old man presents to an ophthalmologist with progressive decrease in his visual acuity over the last 6 months. He also mentions that he has become excessively sensitive to light over the same duration. Past medical history is significant for schizophrenia diagnosed in early adulthood which has been managed with an antipsychotic medication for the past 20 years. The ophthalmologist performs a slit lamp examination and notes discrete brown deposits on the corneal epithelium in both eyes. Which of the following antipsychotic drugs has this patient most likely been taking?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Thioridazine -> Corneal deposits -> 90% CHAIN: Thioridazine -> Pigmentary deposits on cornea -> 85% CHAIN: Thioridazine -> Brownish corneal pigmentation -> 90%
analysis: The presence of discrete brown deposits on the corneal epithelium in both eyes is characteristic of corneal deposits associated with Thioridazine use, a phenomenon known as Thioridazine-induced corneal pigmentation. This patient most likely has been taking Thioridazine.
